evidence.quote:
Fig. 3.
Trends in laboratory findings. At the time of the first administration of T-DXd, inflammatory markers and hepatobiliary enzymes were within normal ranges. On day 17, elevated CRP levels prompted antibiotic therapy initiation. Although CRP levels decreased, γGTP levels continued to rise. On day 49, when symptoms reappeared, elevations in CRP, γGTP, and TB were observed. Despite additional antibiotic administration and placement of an ERBD tube, CRP decreased, while γGTP and TB remained elevated. Hepatic transaminase levels remained within normal limits throughout treatment. Laboratory tests were not performed following the transition to home-based care. The patient died on day 99 of hospitalization. TB, total bilirubin; ERBD, endoscopic retrograde biliary drainage.
